mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines in 80% of 20-day periods but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of those periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.5% indicates a weakening labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST and RSAFS shows no significant predictive power (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns occur in less than 55% of instances where both series decline.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production below 100 (index) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, reducing corporate profits and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or the signal's Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth is positive in 80% of 60-day periods but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of those periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the CPI index exceeding 1.0% signals accelerating inflation, prompting central bank tightening and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises > 1.0% in 3 months, or the signal's Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth and rising unemployment indicate a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline > 0.5% in 3 months and UNRATE rise > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise fails to predict negative returns (S&P 500 positive in >55% of such instances) or the interaction's Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A retail sales figure above 360,000 million dollars indicates strong consumer spending, boosting corporate revenue expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative returns in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS > 360000, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.
